experiments.title: An evolved enzyme enables a later uptake mutation
experiments.hypothesis: In a deliberately constructed nutrient environment, mutation can create and retain a composed enzyme that no existing binary primitive supplies, after which increased uptake becomes advantageous only in the enzyme's presence.
experiments.conclusion: Mixed: the engineered capability barrier was crossed by online mutation, but the registered evolutionary-ratchet criterion was not met. One of 1,825 evaluated compositions passed where all 89 typed primitives failed; B appeared in 3/10 full worlds and persisted in 2/10, while B-only retention passed in only 1/10 against the required 8/10. Both observed B-to-high-uptake events occurred before B's establishment gate, leaving zero eligible candidates and conditional dependence untested, not refuted.
experiments.next_action: Close this fixed matrix without retuning. If revisited, preregister a separate first-clean-B-to-C candidate rule and paired held-out conditional-fitness/removal/restoration test, separating capability discovery from retention conditional on discovery. Do not count the two post hoc early sequences as confirmatory successes; no follow-up worlds have been run.

design.claim_scope: bounded engineered ratchet, not open-ended evolution
design.program_generation: online argument substitution, max two cells

latest_writeup.body_md:
# The barrier was crossed, but the registered ratchet was not demonstrated

This experiment produced an online-generated resource-processing capability outside
the tested primitive repertoire. It did **not** meet the registered conditions for
a reproducible, established-B-then-C evolutionary ratchet. The decisive conditional
fitness assays were not reached, so dependence is **untested**, not disproved.

## What was done

EX-11 introduced a deliberately engineered nutrient into a new controlled Cell80
metabolic world. To exploit it, an organism's program had to compute
`min(65535, a + (a XOR b))` correctly on all 64 registered input pairs. Every one of
the 89 existing stateless binary-u16 primitives failed at least one input. The
claim is specific to this library and interface, not every possible program.

Founders carried only `mask_xor`, with low nutrient uptake. Mutation could generate
two-cell expressions directly at birth from 84 composable primitives; it did not
draw from a pre-screened successful-program pool. High uptake was a separate,
costly allele. Ten seeds each ran full evolution, uptake-disabled (B-only),
no-substrate, and atomic-only controls: 40 worlds, each 3,000 ticks and 256 slots.
The preregistration, code, all changed-genome births, trajectories and state hashes
are retained alongside the analysis.

## What was found

Of 1,825 distinct composed expressions evaluated during mutation, one passed:
`add_sat(a, mask_xor(a,b))`. The same expression arose in multiple worlds; these are
repeated origins, not multiple kinds of innovation. The expression was known to
the experimenter as a validation witness but was not inserted into evolution.
The actual Cell80 tree interpreter and an independent bytecode interpreter agree
on its output over all 64 resource inputs.

In the full arm, this capability appeared in 3/10 worlds and established and
persisted in 2/10. Those two worlds ended with approximately 91% capable organisms
on average over the final 200 ticks. With uptake mutation disabled, it appeared
in 2/10 and established and persisted in 1/10, whose final-window capable fraction
was approximately 81%. The registered B-only retention requirement was **8/10**.

Without substrate, the capability arose in three worlds but established in none.
With composition disabled, it never arose. These controls behaved as expected;
they do not compensate for the failed retention gate.

There were B-then-high-uptake sequences in the two successful full worlds. However,
the uptake changes occurred **19 and 4 ticks before** their B lineage completed
the registered establishment period (at least 20% of slots for 50 consecutive
completed ticks). They were therefore ineligible. No qualifying later candidate
appeared, and the experiment did not substitute these early events after seeing
their outcomes. Zero primary factorial, historical-fork or restoration assays ran.

## What it means

The positive result is narrower but useful: mutation can assemble a capability
that no primitive supplies in this domain, and populations carrying it can spread
and persist in the constructed environment. This goes beyond the earlier
experiment's offline composition pool and immediate-movement novelty checks.

The negative result is failure of the registered overall criterion: reliable
discovery/retention and eligible sequential-candidate supply were insufficient.
The timing observations suggest that the strict establishment-before-C screen
excluded biologically interesting sequences, but that is a **post-run diagnosis**,
not permission to loosen the screen. Candidate eligibility is an evidential rule;
it is not itself a definition of what biological evolution can do.

We have not measured whether those early uptake changes require B for their
fitness advantage in held-out worlds. The energetic design makes that plausible,
but plausibility is not the registered paired removal/restoration evidence.
Nor does this finite, two-cell, experimenter-designed resource demonstrate
open-ended evolution, naturalistic chemistry, or an upgrade of the older
predator/grazer world into a cumulative ecology.

Close this matrix with its unchanged gates. A separate follow-up could preregister
an immediate-first-B→C candidate rule and test clean ancestry plus conditional
fitness directly, while reporting B discovery probability separately from
retention conditional on discovery. That proposal is not run here and must not
turn the present early events into confirmatory evidence.

See [RESULTS.md](RESULTS.md) for every world and [PROVENANCE.md](PROVENANCE.md) for
reproduction and the separation between primary evidence and regression checks.


## Verification and archive

The 40 primary worlds replayed exactly in a separate verification run; only elapsed wall time differs. All 71 distinct tests passed across the full 69-test regression run and the expanded six-test barrier run (four overlapping). The unchanged preregistration SHA-256 is `2ddff28f7e7b4d5813732d363f4b3cc8c5443f0f8937a67194c5448b6da30f61`.

Local reproducibility archive: `ecology-research/experiments/ecology-barrier-bundle.tar.gz`; SHA-256 `f16841bb6b112f9eacacbf210d861a6b2190f4fd2661173c28168d4f0708f1bd`. All 55 manifested source/evidence files were verified against the archived bytes. This is an overlay for Cell80 base `7d61b00719899b449e73c34a90ebbdbae73da19a`, not a standalone workspace or a database attachment. The earlier 379-world closure archive remains unchanged.

experiments.title: A nascent innovation changes the value of a later mutation
experiments.hypothesis: An online-generated resource-processing innovation can make a later uptake mutation beneficial before the innovation completes its establishment period. This dependence should hold both in its birth-time ecology and in standardized held-out worlds.
experiments.conclusion: Mixed, limited support: one online-born B-to-C candidate passed both functional-dependency and historical-opportunity gates before B's operational establishment, but the required three independent discovery cases were not obtained. In that case B was 45 ticks old and occupied 12.5% of slots; both contexts gave B>A in 9/10 futures, BC>B in 10/10, and C-only<=A in 10/10. The child was overwritten during its original birth phase and left zero offspring, so the result supports a conditional selective opportunity, not an accumulated retained causal step. Historical necessity of B, environmental mediation and multi-edge depth remain untested.
experiments.next_action: Close the fixed EX-12 matrix unchanged. Decide whether a separate preregistered follow-up should independently replicate nascent opportunities or test prospective retention/transmission of supported opportunities. Preserve the first-candidate rule and report attrition; do not search later births in this matrix for replacement successes. Reuse the serialized context/intervention ledger, but do not pool identical standardized genotype/seed assays or label an unretained opportunity as accumulated depth.

design.candidate_rule: first clean B-to-C birth, no establishment/outcome filter
design.replicated_success: at least 3 pre-establishment candidates pass both contexts

latest_writeup.body_md:
# EX-12: a supported opportunity, not yet an accumulated step

One online-born, pre-establishment B→C candidate passed the registered dependency
gates in both its birth-time ecology and standardized worlds. This is **limited
support**, not the registered replicated success: three independent discovery
seeds were required, and only one qualified. That candidate also left **zero
offspring in the original history**. We have evidence for a context-specific
selective opportunity, not a retained causal chain or open-ended evolution.

## What was done

The EX-11 ecology, resource barrier, online composition operator, mutation rates,
population size and 3,000-tick horizon were unchanged. EX-12 used 40 new discovery
worlds: ten seeds each for full evolution, B-only, no-substrate and atomic-only.
Candidate selection changed to the first clean B-lineage descendant acquiring
high uptake C, irrespective of establishment or subsequent reproductive success.
The protocol and evidence gates were recorded before fresh seeds were run.

For every selected candidate, we tested A, B, C-only and BC in two distinct
contexts: ten paired continuations from its serialized birth-time snapshot, and
ten separate standardized worlds with ancestral competitors. All these assays
disabled further mutation. The actual pre-B parent program supplied A/C-only.
Each context required B>A, BC>B and positive interaction in at least8/10 futures
and on average, with C-only<=A in at least8/10 and on average. No extinct lineage
or tie was dropped. These are registered screening gates, not calibrated p-values.

The complete record contains 40 discovery worlds, 320 factorial worlds, 80
factorial restorations, four original-history C reversions, four discovery
restorations and four untouched-snapshot continuation checks. Every selected
candidate was tested; none was replaced after failure.

## The supported case

In discovery seed `6840321394656415753` (offset+9), B was born at tick955 and its
clean descendant acquired C at tick1000. B was **45 ticks old**, and its clean
lineage occupied **32/256 slots (12.5%)** immediately before C's birth. The
online-generated enzyme was `add_sat(a,mask_xor(a,b))`, the same capability known
from EX-11, with a new evolutionary origin rather than a seeded genotype.

| Registered contrast | Historical opportunity | Functional dependency |
|---|---:|---:|
| B better than A | 9/10 | 9/10 |
| BC better than B | 10/10 | 10/10 |
| C-only no better than A | 10/10 | 10/10 |
| Positive interaction | 10/10 | 10/10 |

All required mean signs also passed. The mean C-with-B effect was +14,984.2
focal-lineage births in historical continuations and +11,320 in standardized
worlds. Without B, the mean C effect was -0.3 and -6.2, respectively. These are
200-tick descendant-lineage totals, not direct offspring or per-tick fitness.
The designed resource economics strongly favour high uptake after decoding;
this is not a newly discovered biological principle.

## Why the original-history result matters

The passing candidate was overwritten by another birth during the same birth
phase, before it could reproduce. Suppressing its C mutation made no difference
to its descendant count (0 versus0) or the original world's end-of-tick history
hash. A separate post-run audit of the saved pending-parent list and original
counter RNG identifies replacement child3852, parent3838, at slot119.

The historical-opportunity assay keeps the actual birth-time population, nutrient
stocks, location and newborn energy, but samples fresh future randomness and
disables mutation. It therefore establishes a **conditional reproductive
opportunity from that state**. It does not retroactively make the original child
successful, prove an advantage in the exact realized future, or establish
historical necessity of B.

This is the distinction the instrument now makes visible: a genotype can offer
a robust opportunity in controlled futures and still disappear immediately in
the history that actually occurred.

## The other contexts were different

Four first-clean candidates were selected; three preceded operational
establishment. The other pre-establishment candidates arose at clean-B fractions
of63.3% and79.3%, demonstrating why "before the50-tick rule" must not be treated
as synonymous with "rare." They failed the historical gate: B>A in4/10 and6/10,
and BC>B in7/10 for both. The already-established candidate also failed the
historical B>A gate (4/10), despite BC>B in9/10.

All four passed the standardized gate, but **they share the same genotypes and
the same standardized assay seeds**. These are40 distinct genotype/seed assays
executed four times, not160 independent functional tests or four different
innovations. Their historical snapshots are distinct and their effects are
reported separately. We do not pool the two contexts.

Two candidates did leave large descendant lineages in their original worlds,
and their C-only reversions eliminated those particular descendants. Neither
passed both assay contexts. The case passing both contexts was not one of the
historically successful cases. Choosing a later surviving mutation instead would
violate the registered first-candidate rule.

## Discovery was separated from retention

B appeared in5/10 full worlds and established and persisted in4/5 of those.
B-only had the same5/10 discovery and4/5 conditional retention. With no substrate,
B appeared in5/10 and established in0/5. Atomic-only acquired no capability.
These are small-sample, paired-arm observations, not precise probabilities or
proof that innovation supply is the sole bottleneck.

## What the causal ledger can claim

For the offset+9 edge, functional dependency and historical opportunity meet
their registered gates. Historical necessity of B and environmental mediation
remain **untested**. One conditional edge is supported; no two-edge chain has
been tested, and no accumulated retained depth is established by this result.
All four selected first-clean candidates were assayed, but coverage of every
potential causal relationship in these histories is unknown.

EX-12 closes without changing its gates. The next design decision is whether to
prioritize independent replication of nascent opportunities or the retention and
transmission of supported opportunities. A future retention-focused protocol
must select candidates prospectively and report attrition; it cannot rescue this
matrix by searching its later births for successful replacements. Physics,
ecological inheritance and mutation-policy evolution were not introduced.

See [RESULTS.md](RESULTS.md) for every world, [edges.json](edges.json) for the full
context-indexed intervention ledger, and [PROVENANCE.md](PROVENANCE.md) for replay
and reconstruction details.


## Verification and local archive

All 73 regression tests passed with authorized Metal access; the initial sandbox-only GPU failure is retained in the logs. All 452 engine executions of the fixed matrix were repeated, producing byte-identical JSONL; this is verification, not independent replication. Snapshot continuation, exact pre-birth C reversion and restoration checks all passed. The refactored engine also reproduced all 40 EX-11 scientific records unchanged.

Local overlay archive: `ecology-research/experiments/ecology-nascent-bundle.tar.gz`, SHA-256 `6bebe8ca99d472b930c3cb9c89ee3ba8b5a0a25f2a8239546e3a48d84bdab5f7`. All 61 manifested source/evidence files were verified against archived bytes. Base commit: `7d61b00719899b449e73c34a90ebbdbae73da19a`. Raw files remain local, not attached to this database entry. The EX-11 and earlier closure archives remain unchanged.

experiments.title: Can a supported evolutionary opportunity become inherited history?
experiments.hypothesis: A newly born B-to-C opportunity supported by controlled assays can transmit its dependency to descendants that persist in the original mutating ecology. We test whether that dependency remains supported in an intact descendant's ecology 200 ticks later.
experiments.conclusion: Mixed: a supported online B-to-C opportunity transmitted BC and persisted genetically, but no case met the full retained-dependency criterion. Of five first-clean candidates, one passed both birth-context screens; it had 148 intact descendants at +200 and 230 at +500. Its checkpoint dependency effects were positive in 6/10 futures and tied at zero offspring in four, failing the unchanged 8/10 gate without demonstrating a reversal. Full-gate retention was 0/1 supported opportunities (too small to estimate a general probability). The event lineage later went extinct while the capability remained common in other lineages. Accumulation, B's historical necessity and environmental mediation remain untested.
experiments.next_action: Close EX-13 without changing gates or substituting survivors. Before selecting any later D, preregister how to distinguish a genotype's context-specific selective opportunity from its realization probability in single-carrier assays, retaining extinction/ties in unconditional outcomes. Seek independent replication, and keep event-lineage retention separate from continued capability presence in other lineages. Do not treat this checkpoint screen failure as evidence that the dependency reversed.

design.candidate_rule: first clean B-to-C birth, no outcome filter
design.checkpoint_gate: C-with-B positive, C-without-B nonpositive, interaction positive, BC greater than C-only; each >=8/10 and mean sign
design.replicated_success: at least 3 independent retained supported opportunities

latest_writeup.body_md:
# EX-13: transmitted opportunity, unconfirmed retained dependency

A supported B→C opportunity survived, reproduced and produced intact BC
descendants that persisted for hundreds of ticks in the original mutating world.
However, its later-context dependency assay did not meet the registered8/10 gate.
The full retained-edge outcome was therefore **0/1 supported opportunities**,
not replicated support. Accumulation remains **untested**: no later D was assayed.

This is not a replay of EX-12's immediate-loss result. Genetic transmission and
persistence were observed here. Nor does the failed later assay show that the
dependency reversed: its four nonwins were zero-offspring ties across all four
genotypes. One opportunity is far too small a denominator to infer a general
retention probability.

## What was fixed in advance

The ecology, library, online composition operator, mutation rates,256 slots and
3,000-tick discovery horizon were unchanged. Forty fresh worlds ran across full,
B-only, no-substrate and atomic-only arms. The first clean B→C candidate in each
full world was selected at birth without looking at its fate. None was rescued
from contention, replaced by a later survivor or omitted for failing an assay.

Every candidate received the existing dual-context opportunity screen: actual
birth-time ecology plus standardized worlds, ten paired futures each, with all
further mutation disabled. Their unmodified discovery histories continued with
mutation enabled and were traced prospectively.

The primary persistence checkpoint was end of tick C-birth+200. Intact carriers
must retain the exact BC genotype continuously from the selected child; losing
and reacquiring a component does not repair that path. A living descendant was
required, not merely survival of the founder. The lowest-ID intact descendant
was selected before inspecting its future and tested in its actual checkpoint
ecology. No checkpoint candidate was selected for being assay-successful.

The checkpoint required positive C benefit with B, nonpositive C benefit without
B, positive interaction and a positive effect of keeping B in BC, each with the
registered8/10 count and mean sign. Unlike the birth screen, it did not require
B-alone to remain advantageous in the later ecology. This distinction was
registered before any EX-13 outcome, not introduced to rescue a result.

## The supported opportunity and its descendants

The passing birth-opportunity case was seed `6840321394656419844` (offset+4).
B appeared at tick115; the selected C child1124 was born at tick165. B was50 ticks
old and its clean lineage occupied67/256 slots (26.2%), before operational
establishment. The program was the same resource-processing composition as in
EX-11/12, arising online in this fresh world.

The birth-time opportunity assay gave B>A in8/10 futures, BC>B in10/10 and
C-only<=A in10/10; standardized assays gave9/10,10/10 and10/10. Interaction and
all required mean signs also passed.

In the actual mutating history:

- The child survived its birth phase.
- It first reproduced at tick167; its first direct intact BC transmission was
  child1172 at tick169.
- There were217 intact BC descendants at+50 ticks,148 at+200 and230 at+500.
- The+200 checkpoint representative was descendant13943 at the boundary after
  tick365, with its actual position and energy preserved in the assays.

This directly establishes transmission and finite-horizon genetic persistence
of a genotype whose opportunity had passed both birth-context screens.

## The later assay did not pass—but did not show a reversal

For the representative in its checkpoint ecology:

| Contrast | Positive | Tie | Negative | Registered outcome |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| C benefit with B: BC−B | 6 | 4 | 0 | Fails8/10 |
| C benefit without B: C−A | 0 | 10 | 0 | Passes nonpositive gate |
| Interaction | 6 | 4 | 0 | Fails8/10 |
| Removing B from BC: BC−C | 6 | 4 | 0 | Fails8/10 |

The four ties were futures in which **all four focal genotypes produced zero
offspring**. We retained them in the denominator. The mean C-with-B effect was
+421.3 lineage births, but a positive mean did not override the registered
replication requirement. Its median was just1 birth: the mean was dominated by
two much larger lineages. Full paired outcomes are in `edges.json`.

The defensible result is **dependency not supported at the required reliability
in this later context**, not "the biological dependency disappeared." The assay
measures a particular carrier's reproductive outcomes in a particular ecology,
including stochastic loss. It is not a direct, context-free measurement of the
genotype's biochemical requirement.

## Event lineage and capability retention also diverged

The selected C child's entire genealogical lineage became extinct at tick1268.
That does not mean the resource-processing capability disappeared: the world
still had239 capable high-uptake organisms then, and235 at the final tick. Its
final200-tick capable fraction averaged91.9%. These organisms were outside the
selected C child's descendant cohort.

Thus the instrument distinguishes survival of a particular historical origin
from continued presence of the same functional genotype elsewhere. We did not
count another lineage carrying BC as rescue of the selected event, and did not
test whether those other lineages were causally dependent on that event.

## Whole-matrix result and ledger

Five first-clean candidates were selected. All survived, transmitted BC and had
intact descendants at+200. Only one passed BOTH birth-opportunity contexts. One
different candidate passed the checkpoint dependency gate but had failed the
birth-opportunity screen; combining those successes would be invalid.

For the one supported opportunity, the ledger reads:

- opportunity: **supported**;
- transmission: **observed**;
- genetic persistence at+200 and+500: **observed**;
- retained dependency under the full checkpoint criterion: **not supported**;
- accumulation, historical necessity of B and environmental mediation:
  **untested**.

There were no censored supported opportunities. The observed full-gate fraction
is0/1, while transmission and+200 intact persistence were each1/1. Neither is a
precise population probability. Censoring bounds reported by the analyzer concern
missing follow-up in this finite cohort, not sampling uncertainty or confidence.

All five candidates share the same standardized genotype/seed cases:200 executed
standardized assays represent40 distinct cases, not five independent functional
replications. Their historical and checkpoint ecologies are separate contexts.
No multi-edge path was constructed or counted as causal depth.

EX-13 closes with unchanged gates. The next design question is how to distinguish
context-dependent selective opportunity from its probability of realization in
a single-carrier assay, while preserving unconditional reporting of extinction.
Do not discard zero-offspring futures, retrospectively choose another descendant
or infer a later D from genotype persistence. Independent replication and a
prospectively specified measurement design are needed before attempting that
stronger accumulated-chain claim.

See [RESULTS.md](RESULTS.md) for all worlds, [edges.json](edges.json) for the status
ledger and effects, and [PROVENANCE.md](PROVENANCE.md) for verification.


## Verification and archive

All 76 regression tests passed with Metal access. The complete 810-execution EX-13 matrix was repeated byte-for-byte, including prospective cohort traces and checkpoint assays. The preceding EX-12 compatibility matrix was also byte-identical to its sealed primary output. All original birth/checkpoint resume, reversion and restoration checks passed.

Local overlay archive: `ecology-research/experiments/ecology-retention-bundle.tar.gz`; SHA-256 `e893f62ca194a21155f502980b08be26ef93c8e757b8fe37567dc056d32b2f86`. All 63 manifested source/evidence files were verified against archived bytes. Base: `7d61b00719899b449e73c34a90ebbdbae73da19a`. Earlier EX-11, EX-12 and closure archives remain unchanged. Raw files are local, not attached to the database.

experiments.title: Is a transmitted dependency unavailable or merely unrealized?
experiments.hypothesis: In the EX-13 checkpoint ecology, the zero-offspring outcomes reflect stochastic reproductive realization; conditional on either B or BC producing descendants, BC retains a positive selective effect.
experiments.conclusion: Realization-limited: across 100 paired checkpoint futures, B realized births in 41/100 and BC in 64/100. On the preregistered subset where either realized, D=N_BC-N_B was positive in 63/64 futures (mean 99.45, median 4), meeting the 80% conditional-effect gate. A and C-only realized 0/100. Thus EX-13's weak 6/10 checkpoint result was primarily a reproductive-opportunity bottleneck in this ecology, not evidence that the dependency eroded. This remains one transmitted opportunity; accumulation, historical necessity and environmental mediation are untested.
experiments.next_action: Close EX-14. Before attempting D, independently replicate this realization/conditional-effect decomposition across supported opportunities or preregister a cohort-level design. Keep unconditional and conditional quantities separate, and do not treat this one checkpoint as a general Cell80 probability or as accumulated causal depth.

design.conditional_gate: D>0 in >=80% event seeds and positive mean

latest_writeup.body_md: Protocol amendment before execution (2026-09-10): notation was clarified without changing any seed, genotype, horizon, gate or procedure. `N_g` now denotes focal lineage birth count; `I_g = 1[N_g > 0]` denotes binary realization. Unconditional results use `P(I_g=1)` over all 100 futures. Conditional effect is `D = N_BC - N_B`, evaluated only where `I_BC ∨ I_B` is true. This is explicitly a mechanistic decomposition of paired counterfactuals, not another unconditional fitness estimate. Amended preregistration SHA-256: `bd6a3a3fe18362abd42685a5ed5805dce188bf2ad9a24802c7068015770e64ff`.
